items.title: Large Language Model-Based Sentiment Analysis for Public Transit Satisfaction Using Trip Chain Data
items.abstract: This study proposes a methodological framework for analyzing public transit user satisfaction by processing unstructured, voice-derived trip chain data. Traditional survey methods often do not capture the contextual and real time aspects of user experience. To address this limitation, this study employs large language models and natural language processing techniques to analyze trip-related feedback collected from 5,000 public transit users. Sentiment scores were extracted from a station-labeled subset of the data set and applied to a broader corpus to assess satisfaction levels across subway stations in the Seoul Metropolitan Area. Using a combination of sentiment analysis and K-means clustering, this study categorized 102 subway stations into three groups: (1) High Satisfaction Station Group; (2) Low Satisfaction Station Group; and (3) Moderate Satisfaction Station Group. These clusters were the basis for grouping stations, and user feedback on transit experiences was summarized for each station within its respective cluster. This approach enables the identification of low-satisfaction transit stations requiring immediate attention, as well as moderate-satisfaction transit stations where service equity must be addressed. The proposed methodology offers a practical alternative to traditional survey-based assessments by leveraging unstructured public transit users’ data. With further refinement and institutional support, this approach can enhance data-driven, user-centered transit planning and contribute to broader improvements in urban mobility.

items.title: Large Language Models and Applied Surgical Anatomy: Evaluation of Anatomical Reasoning in Expert‐Derived Plastic Surgery Scenarios
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being integrated into medical education, research, and clinical decision‐support applications; however, their ability to apply anatomical knowledge in clinically relevant surgical scenarios remains insufficiently studied. This study evaluated and compared the performance of six contemporary LLMs (ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, DeepSeek, Copilot, and Manus) using 25 expert‐derived applied surgical anatomy scenarios relevant to plastic surgery. Scenarios were developed by an expert panel consisting of one associate professor of anatomy and two plastic surgeons. Responses were generated using a standardized prompt and assessed with a structured scoring rubric evaluating anatomical accuracy, clinical reasoning, completeness, and safety, with a maximum score of 10 points per question. Critical errors were additionally assessed. Significant differences in overall performance were observed among models (Friedman χ 2 = 43.51, p < 0.001). ChatGPT achieved the maximum aggregate score (250/250), followed by Gemini (248/250), DeepSeek (241/250), Copilot (240/250), Claude (235/250), and Manus (219/250). Critical errors were infrequent and were confined to a reconstructive vascular physiology scenario: DeepSeek, Claude, and Manus each demonstrated one observed critical error, whereas ChatGPT, Gemini, and Copilot demonstrated none. Although all evaluated models demonstrated excellent performance, clinically significant anatomical misconceptions persisted despite high aggregate scores. These findings demonstrate strong performance by the tested LLMs on this specific scenario‐based benchmark, while also identifying clinically meaningful anatomical errors in a subset of responses. Future evaluations should focus not only on overall accuracy but also on clinically meaningful error patterns that may influence surgical decision‐making. Importantly, substantial ceiling effects limited discrimination among high‐performing models, and the findings should therefore be interpreted as performance on this specific benchmark rather than as evidence of a general hierarchy of anatomical reasoning capability.

items.title: LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS IN MENTAL HEALTH TRIAGE: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW OF ACCURACY, BIAS, AND ETHICAL DEPLOYMENT ACROSS DIGITAL PLATFORMS
items.abstract: Background: The intersection of a global psychiatric workforce shortage and the rapid advancement of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) has catalyzed the integration of Large Language Models (LLMs) into digital healthcare. LLMs are increasingly deployed as preliminary triage agents to assess psychological distress, yet their diagnostic reliability, demographic neutrality, and safety protocols in crisis scenarios remain heavily debated within the psychiatric community. Objective: This review evaluates current research to determine the trustworthiness of large language models (LLMs) used in psychiatric screening. In doing so, it shines a light on the algorithmic biases present in practical use and maps out the necessary ethical standards to ensure digital health services remain safe and fair for all patients. Methodology: We sourced peer-reviewed publications released between 2023 and 2026 by running a systematic literature search across Google Scholar, PubMed/MEDLINE, and IEEE Xplore. The synthesis focused on comparative accuracy studies, observational evaluations, and sociotechnical analyses of leading LLMs (e.g., GPT-4, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, Gemini 1.5 Pro) applied specifically to psychiatric screening and automated clinical routing. Results: LLMs demonstrate high diagnostic concordance with human clinicians in structured assessments for high-prevalence conditions like major depressive disorder, effectively parsing unstructured clinical narratives. However, they exhibit a consistent tendency toward conservative over-triage in psychiatric emergencies. Profound algorithmic biases persist; models frequently recommend divergent, often inferior, treatment pathways for marginalized demographic groups and display gender-based stigmatization. Furthermore, models struggle with complex psychopathologies and display inconsistent safety mechanisms during acute suicidal ideation queries. Conclusion: While LLMs offer substantial utility for scaling preliminary psychiatric screening and reducing administrative triage burdens, their propensity for factual hallucination, demographic bias, and uncalibrated risk escalation currently precludes autonomous clinical deployment. Robust, human-in-the-loop governance and culturally representative training corpora are imperative prior to further integration into global digital health ecosystems.

items.title: Large language models in personalized oncology
items.abstract: Background . Large language models are considered a promising tool for personalized oncology; however, their role in the analysis of molecular data and treatment selection should be clearly distinguished from the functions of specialized predictive models. Objective . To systematize the potential applications of large language models in personalized oncology, primarily for the interpretation of clinical, genomic, and transcriptomic data and of predictions of tumor chemo- and radiosensitivity. Methods . We performed a narrative review of publications identified in PubMed and Google Scholar, with the search updated through July 1, 2026. Original studies and reviews on medical LLM applications, foundation models for genomic and transcriptomic data, clinical decision support, and prediction of anticancer treatment sensitivity were considered. Results . The most justified approach is to use a language model as an interface layer: a specialized machine-learning or deep-learning model calculates the prediction, while the language model generates an explanation, compares the result with clinical guidelines, and indicates limitations. The main risks include unreliable responses, insufficient reproducibility, weak external validation, and legal constraints. Conclusion . A clinically promising architecture separates computation from explanation: the language model does not prescribe treatment autonomously but links molecular data, a validated predictive model, and the physician.

items.title: Leadership as a Service? Delegating Leadership Functions to Agentic AI—Boundaries, Risks and Accountabilities
items.abstract: Leadership is increasingly delivered, in part, by software. Agentic artificial intelligence (AI) systems now monitor team activity, coordinate work across people and tools, schedule and assign tasks, deliver feedback and performance nudges, and broker information between leaders and followers — functions that organisations once obtained only from human managers. This has prompted the suggestion that leadership itself is becoming a service: a set of functions that can be specified, subscribed to and supplied by systems rather than embodied in persons. This conceptual paper examines that suggestion critically. Drawing on functional leadership theory, the automation–augmentation paradox, and the literature on algorithmic management and trust in AI, I develop a function-by-delegability framework that classifies five leadership functions — sensing and monitoring, coordination, deciding and allocating, developing and giving feedback, and representing and meaning-making — according to how far each can responsibly be delegated to agentic systems. I argue that delegability is governed less by technical capability than by accountability: I introduce the accountability floor, the principle that functions whose delegation would break the chain of accountability may be automated in execution but never in ownership. I identify four risks of delegation — legitimacy and follower trust, bias at scale, accountability gaps, and erosion of the leadership pipeline — propose governance and design principles, and derive three propositions for empirical research.

items.title: Leading Inclusively: Universal Design Principles in the Age of AI
items.abstract: Modern organizational leaders increasingly encounter artificial intelligence (AI) technologies in their workplaces, creating both opportunities and challenges for inclusive leadership. This chapter introduces Universal Design for Learning (UDL) as a framework for navigating these technological changes while maintaining human-centered approaches to inclusion. UDL’s three core principles – multiple means of representation, engagement, and action/expression – provide leaders with practical strategies for creating flexible workplace systems that benefit all employees. When thoughtfully implemented, AI technologies can support these principles through personalized learning experiences, enhanced accessibility features, and improved communication tools. However, the chapter cautions leaders to ensure that technology is amplifying rather than replacing human judgment and cultural competence. The chapter addresses critical considerations for leaders, including the risks of algorithmic bias, the limitations of automated solutions in complex interpersonal situations, and the importance of maintaining employee agency and choice. It examines common implementation barriers – from cost concerns to misconceptions about technology as a cure-all for inclusion challenges – while demonstrating that UDL principles require minimal investment and generate significant returns. Through examination of both opportunities and pitfalls, leaders learn to distinguish between technological applications that enhance inclusion and those that may inadvertently create barriers. The chapter provides actionable guidance for implementing UDL principles in technology-enhanced environments, positioning inclusive leadership capabilities as essential competencies for organizational success regardless of technological context.

items.title: Learning to Remember: Advances in Memory Mechanisms for Large Language Models
items.abstract: Memory has become a central mechanism for extending large language models (LLMs) beyond fixed context windows, stateless interaction, and static parametric knowledge. This survey organizes the literature around three complementary dimensions: the life cycle of memory, the storage substrate, and the system role that memory plays in LLM-based agents, while using cognitive-science-inspired memory concepts as a lightweight conceptual motivation rather than as a separate technical contribution or implementation family. On this basis, we distinguish three mechanism families: nonparametric memory, where information is stored outside model parameters in text, graph, multimodal, or database-like structures; parametric memory, where information is stored or accessed through activations, key-value caches, learned modules, adapter-based parameterizations, or model weights; and memory for agent evolution, where stored experiences support reinforcement learning, continual learning, procedural reuse, context engineering, and agent harness design. Evaluation is treated as a separate cross-cutting component rather than as a memory mechanism. Unlike surveys that focus primarily on retrieval-augmented generation or long-context modeling, this paper emphasizes the full memory life cycle: construction, maintenance, retrieval, consolidation, forgetting, governance, and evaluation. By aligning conceptual motivations, computational memory mechanisms, benchmarks, and deployment concerns, the survey provides a structured roadmap for designing memory-augmented LLM agents that are persistent, adaptive, auditable, and safe to update over time.

items.title: Learning When to Commit: Schedule Distillation for Fast Diffusion Language Models
items.abstract: Diffusion large language models (dLLMs) can generate multiple tokens in parallel, but often require many decoding rounds to complete a response. Efficient generation depends not only on which tokens are easy to predict, but also on how committing to them helps predict the remaining positions. A highly predictable token may provide little useful context, while revealing a less predictable token can help several other positions become predictable sooner. We propose dSpark, a new schedule distillation-based framework for learning when to commit tokens for faster diffusion language generation. To achieve this, we construct unmasking schedules that prioritize tokens whose reveal makes other positions easier to predict, reducing uncertainty earlier in decoding. We then distill these schedules into the model to enable faster parallel sampling, with a KL-divergence regularizer to help preserve generation quality. We extensively evaluate our approach across mathematical reasoning and code generation tasks. On GSM8K, our method achieves remarkable 10.12$\times$ and 5.12$\times$ speedups over the various baselines on LLaDA-8B-Instruct and Dream-7B-Instruct, respectively, while maintaining superior task performance. Our code is available at https://github.com/VILA-Lab/dSpark.

items.title: Legal Priorities for the Development of Artificial Intelligence and Their Implementation in the Sphere of Education
items.abstract: The paper examines the conceptual foundations of the legal regulation of artificial intelligence and the possibilities of their application to the education system. The initial premise of the work is the proposition that AI has ceased to be a private technical instrument and has turned into an infrastructural technology that defines a new socio-political era and generates constitutional challenges of a systemic, synergetic and existential nature. The author identifies the key threats: the substitution of democratic institutions by algorithmic governance, technologically conditioned inequality and algorithmic discrimination, micro-manipulation of the information flow, and the concentration of power resources among the holders of algorithms. As a meta-threat, the challenge to the socio-humanistic paradigm is considered, associated with the choice between transhumanism and classical humanism. By way of discussion, eight principles of the legal regulation of AI are formulated: state strategic guidance and technological integrity; guaranteed protection of the affected person and enhanced liability; "human in the loop" in critical decisions; anthropological priority; digital equality and the prohibition of discrimination; respect for dignity and non-interference in the private sphere; managed transparency; technological neutrality and anticipatory regulation. Further, these principles are projected onto the sphere of education. The author distinguishes two modalities of the use of AI — "a simulator for the mind" and "a prosthesis for laziness" — and shows that legal regulation must establish the boundaries of the permissible application of the technology. The legal risks of algorithmic assessment are analyzed, along with the problem of the right to explanation and the protection of the student from unfounded accusations, digital inequality in access to AI tools, threats to privacy and dignity, as well as the question of the status of the educator as a condition for the humanistic development of AI. A conclusion is drawn regarding the necessity of building a system of requirements for transparency, accountability, equality of access and the preservation of human control in critical decisions.

items.title: LifeUML: A Declarative Domain-Specific Language and Mathematical Formulation for Human Mobility and Career Architecture
items.abstract: Cross-border mobility and career pivoting represent high-stakes, multi-variable optimization challenges traditionally hindered by qualitative ambiguity, subjective counseling, and disconnected legal-financial silos. In this paper, we introduce LifeUML, a formal, declarative domain-specific language (DSL) and deterministic mathematical formulation engineered to model human life trajectories, cross-border solvency runway, and global immigration feasibility. Inspired by the declarative abstraction paradigms of UML and PlantUML, LifeUML enables autonomous AI agents and individuals to compile human aspirations into structured Abstract Syntax Trees (ASTs) that are evaluated in-browser against empirical psychometrics (IPIP Big-Five, Holland RIASEC) and verified 2026 sovereign statutory immigration gazettes across 40 jurisdictions. We formalize four core computational metrics: (1) the Life Mobility Index (LMI), evaluating legal solvency margins, emergency cash runways, fiscal retention, and cross-cultural adaptability; (2) the AI Transformation Quotient (AX-Q), quantifying autonomous digital leverage; (3) the Dream Convergence Index (DCI), modeling high-dimensional cosine aptitude alignment against target innovation clusters; and (4) an exponential temporal willpower decay model (C(t) = C0 * exp(-lambda * t)) that enforces deterministic action-locking. We further delineate comprehensive legal and ethical safeguards: a clean-room TypeScript parser ensuring copyright independence, public-domain psychometric foundations that bypass proprietary trademark liabilities, statutory delta calculations that prevent the unauthorized practice of law (UPL), and zero-server client-side execution complying with EU AI Act (2024/1689) high-risk employment exemptions.

items.abstract: Digital literacy has become an important competence for university students writing academic papers, particularly in the final semester when they prepare articles, research proposals, or undergraduate theses. Digital literacy involves more than operating devices; it also includes searching for information, evaluating source credibility, managing references, composing texts, and using technology ethically. This article examines how digital literacy supports the academic writing skills of eighth-semester students through a literature review. A narrative literature review was conducted by examining relevant journal articles available online. Sources were selected based on topical relevance, their connection to higher education students, and the availability of bibliographic information and accessible abstracts or full texts. The review indicates that digital literacy supports writing through access to scholarly sources, information evaluation, the use of word-processing and reference-management applications, and more efficient revision. These benefits, however, require critical thinking, knowledge of academic conventions, and ethical technology use, including the use of artificial intelligence. Therefore, digital literacy development should be integrated with reading habits, writing practice, lecturer guidance, and academic integrity.

items.title: LLM Hallucination Detection via Low-rank Multilinear Decomposition
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) frequently generate fluent yet factually incorrect responses, raising concerns about their reliability. Recent hallucination detectors increasingly exploit internal representations, but extracting informative signals from high-dimensional hidden states remains challenging. Existing approaches often rely on selected activations or pooling-based compression, potentially overlooking discriminative information distributed across Transformer layers, feature modes, and tokens. We propose LOTUS (Low-rank Order-statistic TUcker-based Subspace learning), a multilinear low-rank decomposition framework for hallucination detection that extracts compact representations from LLM hidden states while reducing dependence on labeled data. Our approach first summarizes variable-length token representations using complementary statistical descriptors that capture peak activations, activation distributions, and cross-layer changes. We then leverage low-rank multilinear decomposition to extract compact representations that capture the underlying structure of LLM hidden states, which are subsequently used to train a lightweight hallucination classifier. Experiments across multiple LLMs and question-answering benchmarks demonstrate improved hallucination detection performance over recent state-of-the-art baselines.

items.title: LLM-Based Agentic AI in Manufacturing: A Scoping Review of Applications, System Designs and Evaluation Practices
items.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly used in manufacturing to design products, plan production, diagnose faults and operate equipment, but their designs and evaluations remain difficult to compare. We analyse 164 studies identified through Scopus, Web of Science and IEEE Xplore to examine manufacturing applications, agentic system designs and evaluation practices, and to identify where evaluation coverage falls short of the evidence that these task and design types would require. We propose taxonomies of applications, agentic designs and evaluation practices, and relate task and design characteristics to the evidence required to assess them. The findings reveal an imbalance between assessing output quality and verifying whether outputs satisfy manufacturing requirements. For planning and decision-making systems, executability and constraint compliance receive limited evaluation, while most evidence comes from offline data or simulation. Limited assessment of safety, stability across repeated runs and performance in industrial settings leaves a gap between demonstrated task performance and evidence of reliable operation under manufacturing conditions. The resulting taxonomies and evidence requirements help researchers select evaluations suited to each manufacturing use case and distinguish demonstrated task performance from evidence of reliable operation.

items.title: LLM-Based Fuzzy Agent for Human–Machine Interaction in STEM Education and Taiwanese-English Co-Learning Application
items.abstract: Abstract This paper presents a Large Language Model (LLM)-based fuzzy agent framework designed to enhance Human-Machine Interaction (HMI) in Quantum Computational Intelligence (QCI) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) learning, as well as Taiwanese-English co-learning. By integrating QCI&AI STEM experiential learning with language co-learning applications, the framework creates an adaptive and personalized learning environment using fuzzy logic-based Human Intelligence (HI) and evolutionary computation-based Machine Intelligence (MI). The framework comprises three main components: (1) the QCI&AI STEM experiential learning agent, which integrates QCI software and AI-driven models to facilitate interactive STEM learning; (2) the Trustworthy AI Dialogue Engine (TAIDE)-based Taiwanese-English co-learning agent, which utilizes the Meta AI USTmodel, TAIDE, and fine-tuned Open AI Whisper-Taiwanese model for real-time Taiwanese-English co-learning; and (3) the fuzzy Knowledge Graph (KG) agent, which constructs teacher’s and learners’ knowledge graphs to evaluate the students’ learning performance. Besides, an HMI-based Observation with Comfortable Intelligence (HMI-OwCI) model is proposed to create intelligent technologies that are seamlessly integrated and intuitively aligned with human needs. Additionally, two supporting agents enhance the proposed framework: the Genetic Algorithm-based Neural Network (GANN) Agent, which optimizes QCI learning models, and the LLM fine-tuned agent, which refines Taiwanese-English co-learning and generates various Whisper-Taiwanese models. Experimental results highlight that GANN adapts well in QCI&AI STEM learning, Whisper-Taiwanesemodels generalize effectively, and the fuzzy KG agent enables adaptive learning assessments.

items.title: LLM-Enhanced Heterogeneous Graph Learning with Business Semantics for Financial Fraud Detection
items.abstract: Financial fraud detection increasingly relies on heterogeneous transaction graphs, in which entities such as cards and merchants play distinct business roles and the risk meaning of an attribute depends on the entity's role: a high transaction volume may be routine for a merchant but unusual for a card. Heterogeneous graph neural networks preserve typed entities and relations but typically treat these attributes as role-agnostic inputs and leave their business meaning implicit. Meanwhile, most existing methods integrating large language models (LLMs) with graphs focus on homogeneous graphs or heterogeneous graphs with naturally available textual attributes, leaving their use on transaction graphs with structured attributes underexplored. To address this issue, we propose SemHGT, an LLM-enhanced framework that interprets structured attributes according to entity roles and makes the business semantics explicit in three stages: (1) role-aware prompts elicit risk-related business descriptions from node attributes, and a text encoder maps them to semantic vectors that enrich node representations; (2) semantic similarity guides multi-round sampling of target-specific path instances under transaction-to-transaction schemas; (3) schema-level tokens that combine local path evidence with global neighbor summaries are processed together with the target transaction by a unified transformer. Across three benchmark datasets, SemHGT leads the evaluated baselines on most dataset--metric comparisons. Further analyses provide additional evidence for the effectiveness of SemHGT's design and clarify how its semantic modeling and evidence selection contribute to fraud detection. Code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/SemHGT-528A/.

items.title: LongSearchEval: Evaluating Long-Horizon Web Search Capabilities of Large Language Models via a Trajectory-Aware Agent Framework with Failure-Node Localization
items.abstract: Long-horizon web search requires LLM-based agents to integrate information across web pages through extended interactions under task-specific constraints. Evaluating this capability is important not only for measuring final answer quality, but also for assessing whether an agent acquires, verifies, and uses evidence reliably over extended interactions. Existing evaluations, however, mainly rely on simulated trajectories or on post-hoc trajectories reconstructed from final answers, rather than on retained real interaction traces, which limits the fidelity of behavioral assessment and weakens support for fine-grained error localization. To address this gap, we introduce LONGSEARCHEVAL, a trajectory-aware agent evaluation framework that combines a unified agent execution protocol with source constrained outcome verification and retrospective failure-node localization. Stage 1 verifies answer groups against agent-cited webpages without human-authored gold answers; Stage 2 audits normalized rounds and links flagged failure nodes to incorrect answer groups. We evaluate 16 models from eight families on 100 tasks, yielding 1,600 retained runs and 6,545 automatically flagged failure nodes. Trajectory collection and evaluation required 1,037 and 318 hours of cumulative runtime, respectively. Human validation yields 94.50% agreement on supplied answer-group labels and 98.11% feature-correspondence precision for audited round-group links. Together, outcome scores and linked trajectory evidence support controlled model comparison and retrospective inspection of answer-related content.

items.title: LoRA on a Budget: Function-Aware Post-Hoc Compression for Adapter Fleets
items.abstract: Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) has become a key mechanism for efficiently specializing foundation models into many task- and user-specific variants. Serving many LoRA adapters under a shared resource budget turns post-hoc compression into a two-level allocation problem: rank must be distributed across layers within each adapter and across adapters within the fleet. Although trained LoRAs contain substantial spectral redundancy, spectral reconstruction alone does not determine how much compression an adapter can functionally tolerate. We formulate fleet compression through a functional rank-distortion frontier for each adapter, followed by fleet-level minimax allocation under a shared rank budget. Given exact frontiers, this decomposition is equivalent to joint optimization over all layer ranks. We introduce Functional Rank Allocation (FRA), an unlabeled method for constructing practical frontiers. FRA measures isolated module truncations end to end, uses these measurements as an additive search surrogate solved by dynamic programming, remeasures every complete candidate, and takes the lower-risk envelope with a complementary spectral proposal before exact minimax allocation over the constructed frontiers. Across 78 adapters from three public fleets, FRA improves worst-case and tail utility over uniform spectral compression in constrained-budget regimes. Fixed-budget probes show that isolated costs rank candidates well, but their calibration shifts across proposal shapes; end-to-end verification and the spectral proposal therefore limit functional-search error.

items.title: Machine learning over encrypted data: a survey of fully homomorphic encryption for AI systems
items.abstract: The increasing use of machine learning (ML) in privacy-sensitive domains such as healthcare, finance, and user-facing services has intensified the need for techniques that enable data-driven intelligence without exposing sensitive information. Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) offers a cryptographically rigorous approach to privacy-preserving machine learning by allowing computations to be performed directly on encrypted data. While appealing in principle, the integration of FHE into modern ML pipelines introduces substantial challenges that fundamentally affect model design, algorithm selection, and system performance. This survey provides a comprehensive and structured review of machine learning over encrypted data using non-interactive FHE-based approaches. We examine how a wide range of machine learning models, including traditional ML algorithms, deep neural networks, and emerging transformer architectures, are adapted to operate under the arithmetic, precision, and efficiency constraints imposed by FHE. To organize a rapidly growing body of work, we introduce a unifying taxonomy that captures key design dimensions such as encryption schemes, nonlinearity handling strategies, model families, system-level optimizations, and privacy objectives. Using this framework, we synthesize existing approaches, analyze trade-offs between accuracy, efficiency, and security, and highlight recurring design patterns across the literature. Beyond summarizing existing techniques, this survey discusses practical limitations, deployment considerations, and open research challenges that shape the future of privacy-preserving machine learning under encryption. By bridging cryptographic techniques and modern AI system design, this work aims to serve as a reference for researchers and practitioners seeking to develop secure, scalable, and trustworthy machine learning systems.

items.title: Machine learning-based assessment of tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes in breast cancer histopathology: a systematic review and evidence-gap analysis of translational readiness
items.abstract: Background Machine learning-based assessment of tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TILs) has been proposed to improve the reproducibility and clinical utility of immune-contexture evaluation in breast cancer histopathology. However, existing studies differ substantially in task definition, annotation strategy, model architecture, validation design, and clinical endpoint. This systematic review and evidence-gap analysis aimed to map the translational readiness of TIL-related machine learning studies in breast cancer histopathology and to identify cluster-specific methodological gaps. Methods A systematic search of PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, ScienceDirect, and Google Scholar was conducted up to 20 April 2026, supplemented by backward citation tracing and a targeted Google search of the 30 most relevant additional results. Eligible studies included breast cancer histopathology-based machine learning, deep learning, artificial intelligence, or computational image-analysis studies evaluating TILs or TIL-related immune-cell features. Studies were grouped by principal application into detection/classification, outcome prognostication, and treatment-response prediction. Extracted variables included data source, specimen type, model family, annotation strategy, validation design, clinical comparator use, calibration, decision-curve analysis, incremental value, reproducibility, and methodological challenges. Because of heterogeneity in endpoints and performance metrics, synthesis was descriptive and evidence-map based. Results The primary evidence map included 51 histopathology-image studies: 19 detection/classification, 18 outcome prognostication, and 14 treatment-response prediction studies. External validation was reported in 31.6% of detection/classification studies, 61.1% of prognostication studies, and 57.1% of treatment-response prediction studies. Clinical comparator reporting increased across the same continuum, from 63.2% to 94.4% and 92.9%, respectively. However, calibration was reported in only one prognostication study (5.6%) and in no detection/classification or treatment-response prediction studies. Decision-curve analysis was similarly limited to one prognostication study. Class imbalance was near-universal (94.7–100% across clusters). Scanner/stain robustness was addressed in a majority of studies (63.2–83.3%), but fairness or subgroup analyses remained inconsistently reported (27.8–57.1%). Conclusions TIL machine learning in breast cancer is technically active but clinically under-validated. Future studies should move beyond model development toward externally validated, calibrated, clinically benchmarked, reproducible, and decision-relevant evidence, using cluster-specific planning standards for detection, prognostication, and treatment-response prediction. items.title: Making pandemics public: COVID-19 dashboards, health security and popular communication
items.abstract: Real-time dashboards were one of the emblematic features of the COVID-19 pandemic. This article analyses dashboards as popular media of situational awareness. After developing an analytics of the popular inspired by systems theory and deconstruction, we highlight three points. First, the proliferation of the dashboard can be understood against the backdrop of a liberal biopolitics of health emergencies. Under liberal conditions, public health officials depend on the cooperation of the population, which is why communicating the situation is a central element of crisis management in pandemics. Second, the dashboard can be understood as a technical solution to the communication challenges associated with lay audiences. From the perspective of those responsible, laypeople have difficulty correctly interpreting scientific data on the pandemic, which is why alternative forms of representation and communication are needed. Finally, we highlight the affective dimension of dashboard inclusion. The aesthetic of the dashboard is observed as an affective tool that is capable of fascinating the public even before any meaning is processed. On the one hand, this fascination fosters inclusion, as it binds the viewer more strongly to the events. However, it also becomes problematic when aesthetic dramatization threatens to undermine the subjectification of a pandemic citizenship.

items.title: Management Information System Innovation And Implementation Suitability In Managerial Decision Making
items.abstract: General Background Technological advancements mandate hospitals to integrate reliable administration systems for providing accountable healthcare services. Specific Background Hospital Management Information Systems supply crucial data assisting leaders in operational planning and strategic policy formulation. Knowledge Gap Although previous studies correlate system usage with staff performance, research simultaneously integrating information quality, operational capability, and system suitability toward managerial choices remains limited. Aims This study investigates how information quality, user competence, and implementation suitability determine managerial decision-making at RSUD Karangkembang Lamongan. Results Quantitative analysis of 30 employees using multiple linear regression reveals that information quality and user competence partially demonstrate no significant relationship with decision-making. Conversely, implementation suitability displays a positive and significant relationship. Simultaneously, all three variables determine 78.8% of the decision-making variance, establishing implementation suitability as the most dominant determinant. Novelty This research explicitly shifts the analytical focus from general clinical performance to the integration of systemic, human, and organizational factors driving strategic managerial choices. Implications Hospital administrators must prioritize aligning system features with organizational workflows rather than solely focusing on technical training or data availability to ensure optimal strategic planning. Highlights Workflow alignment acts as the dominant determinant for strategic planning operations. Technical competence alone does not directly guarantee better organizational choices without workflow synchronization. Systemic and human factors collectively determine a massive proportion of strategic choice variance. items.title: Mapping institutional change research in higher education: A BERTopic-based topic modelling study
items.abstract: Research on institutional change in higher education has grown quickly, but it remains fragmented across disciplines and theoretical traditions. This study maps the thematic structure of this research in educational sciences and traces how it has changed over 34 years. I analysed the titles and abstracts of 2,623 publications indexed in the Web of Science Core Collection (Education & Educational Research, 1992–2025) with BERTopic, an embedding-based topic modelling tool. Placeholder masking kept the names of countries, nationalities and languages from shaping the topics, and key model settings are reported for reproducibility. The model produced 24 interpretable topics covering 1,824 publications. The general Structural Reforms topic fell from 65.6% of topic-assigned publications in 1992–2000 to 12.5% in 2023–2025, while more specific themes such as sustainability, transformational leadership and diversity, equity and inclusion gained weight. In 2023–2025, Digital Transformation became the largest topic (14.8%), and Artificial Intelligence Integration rose from almost zero to 8.1%. Technology-related research developed in successive waves: e-learning, emergency remote teaching during the COVID-19 pandemic, digital transformation and generative artificial intelligence. Each wave reframed digitalisation with new concepts instead of simply continuing the previous one. These results suggest that institutional change in higher education is studied through several parallel pathways rather than a single dominant narrative. For policymakers and institutional leaders, the findings point to the need to build the capacity for change as a lasting institutional capability rather than responding to each technological, sociological and political disruption separately.

items.title: Mapping interdependencies among challenges to artificial intelligence adoption in drug discovery
items.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) offers significant potential to accelerate drug discovery, yet its adoption remains constrained by interdependent technical, organizational, and regulatory barriers. This study applies Fuzzy DEMATEL to analyze twelve challenges and uncover their causal structure using expert judgments expressed as triangular fuzzy numbers. Following normalization and CFCS defuzzification, Resistance to Change, Lack of Standardization, Limited Trust in AI Outputs, Talent Shortage, and Lack of Clinical Validation emerge as the primary causal drivers. These upstream barriers exert strong influence on downstream effects, including Regulatory Barriers, Biological Complexity, Integration with Legacy Systems, and Poor Data Quality. The findings indicate that several constraints commonly viewed as external are, in practice, manifestations of internal organizational and technical shortcomings. By providing a structured causal prioritization of barriers, this study offers actionable guidance for targeting high-leverage interventions in AI-enabled drug discovery. Findings reflect expert judgment within a North Cyprus context and should be interpreted as indicative organizational signals rather than universal prescriptions.

items.title: Mapping the evolution of artificial intelligence in atmospheric aerosol research: a bibliometric and text-mining analysis
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has become increasingly important in atmospheric aerosol and particulate-matter (PM) research because it can model nonlinear relationships, integrate heterogeneous observations, and generate high-resolution spatiotemporal information. This study maps the evolution and knowledge structure of AI-based atmospheric aerosol and PM research using 4,872 Web of Science (WoS) publications published through December 31, 2025. Bibliometric and text-mining analyses were used to characterize publication trends, leading countries and institutions, major journals, citation patterns, keyword co-occurrence networks, and abstract-based thematic clusters. In addition, 99 publications indexed in the Korea Citation Index (KCI) were examined separately to provide supplementary context on temporal publication trends in the Korean domestic literature. WoS publication activity increased sharply after 2019, with China contributing the largest publication output and total citation count, while several lower-output countries showed higher mean citations per publication. Keyword-network analysis identified machine learning as a central theme linking PM prediction, deep learning, aerosol optical depth, exposure assessment, and satellite remote sensing. Abstract-based clustering revealed five major thematic domains spanning prediction modeling, PM concentration and exposure, satellite-based aerosol retrieval, emission-related analysis, and aerosol monitoring and environmental applications. The results indicate a shift from model-specific prediction toward multisource integration, spatiotemporal analysis, remote sensing, and exposure-oriented applications. These findings provide a structured overview of the field and highlight the need for more interpretable, uncertainty-aware, and transferable AI approaches.

items.title: MAREval: A Multi-Agent Framework for Evaluating Natural Language Recommendation Explanations
items.abstract: Evaluating natural language explanations in recommender systems is essential for fostering user trust, transparency, and engagement. However, existing evaluation approaches like human evaluations, while accurate, are resource-intensive and impractical at the scale required by modern recommendation platforms. Also, automated methods using single-agent LLMs suffer from prompt sensitivity and inconsistent outputs. To address these challenges, we propose MAREval, a structured multi-agent framework for evaluating recommendation explanations using large language models. MAREval orchestrates (i) a planner agent that uses a novel Chain of Debate (CoD) prompting strategy to coordinate agent roles and enforce logically consistent evaluation plans; (ii) a moderator agent that regulates discussions by mitigating prompt drift; and (iii) an arbitrator agent that aggregates outputs from multiple evaluation rounds and (iv) a Monte Carlo sampling method, improving robustness and alignment with human judgment. We conduct comprehensive evaluations on both public (TopicalChat) and proprietary recommendation datasets, demonstrating that MAREval outperforms state-of-the-art baselines. Comprehensive experiments on a public benchmark and a proprietary e-commerce dataset show that MAREval improves alignment with human judgments over strong singleand multi-agent baselines. Stability analyses indicate substantially lower variability across repeated trials. In a large human-annotation gate, MAREval meets production quality thresholds where prior evaluators fall short, and online A/B testing demonstrates statistically significant improvements in engagement and revenue metrics. These results establish MAREval as a scalable and reliable solution for human-aligned evaluation of recommendation explanations in real-world systems

items.title: MARQ: A Modular, LLM-Agnostic Requirement Quality Assessor Infused with Systems Engineering Knowledge
items.abstract: Requirements engineering (RE) is foundational to systems engineering (SE), as requirement defects can propagate downstream and adversely affect development outcomes. Although large language models (LLMs) are promising for requirement quality assessment, prior work shows that off-the-shelf models miss a large share of expert-identified defects, perform unevenly across quality criteria, and vary across executions. This study investigates whether infusing expert-derived SE knowledge can improve LLM-based requirement quality evaluation beyond off-the-shelf capability. We present MARQ, a modular, LLM-agnostic prototype that supplements LLMs with a criterion-specific knowledge stack operationalizing INCOSE requirement quality criteria and evaluated against off-the-shelf baselines on an expert-labeled NASA requirement set using Claude Opus 5, GPT-5.6 Sol, and the open-weight Gemma 3 12B, with 100 executions per model. MARQ achieves median F1 scores of 0.80 for Claude Opus 5, 0.62 for GPT-5.6 Sol, and 0.53 for Gemma 3 12B, compared with off-the-shelf baselines of 0.55, 0.52, and 0.18, respectively. However, the nature of these gains is model-dependent. Claude Opus 5 improves defect detection and false-alarm control; GPT-5.6 Sol gains detection and better execution-level consistency at the cost of more false alarms; and Gemma 3 12B reaches the performance of off-the-shelf proprietary models, although it remains highly variable. Criterion-level analysis shows gains concentrated in Correctness and Conformance, trade-offs between misses and false alarms within individual criteria, and model-dependent responses across several criteria. These findings position SE knowledge infusion as a promising model-agnostic pathway for strengthening trustworthy LLM-based RE support while underscoring the need for criterion-specific interventions and human-in-the-loop review.

items.title: MATCHA: A Chinese Multi-Disorder Mental Health Dataset with Cross-Lingual Analyses on Social Media
items.abstract: Mental health research on social media has been dominated by English-language datasets and DSM-5-centered resources, limiting cross-lingual and cross-cultural understanding of online mental health expression. We introduce MATCHA, the first Chinese multi-disorder mental health dataset that links disorder-specific Weibo Super-Topic communities with users' broader public timelines. MATCHA covers seven DSM-5 disorders and a control group, comprising 46,025 cohort-level users and 1.8 million posts. The dataset distinguishes users with explicit self-disclosure evidence from broader disorder-related participants through an LLM-assisted annotation pipeline, and is released in a rigorously de-identified, controlled-access format. Using MATCHA, we analyze behavioral, linguistic, symptom-related, and life-event-related patterns across disorders, and conduct cross-lingual comparisons with Twitter-STMHD. Our analyses show that Weibo Super-Topics function as concentrated spaces for affective and health-related expression, while cross-platform differences between Weibo and Twitter often exceed cross-disorder variation. MATCHA provides a new resource for community-aware and cross-lingual mental health NLP research.

items.title: Mathematics Teachers’ Pedagogical Evaluations of Artificial Intelligence in Mathematics Education: Opportunities, Risks, and Classroom Positioning
items.abstract: This study aimed to examine how mathematics teachers in public schools in Türkiye evaluate the role of artificial intelligence (AI) in mathematics teaching. The accuracy and pedagogical suitability of AI-generated content make such judgments important in mathematics education. Designed as a qualitative case study, the research focused on seven teachers drawn from a broader maximum variation sample. Participants varied in years of teaching experience, graduate education, and self-reported AI experience. Data were collected through semi-structured online interviews and analyzed using descriptive content analysis focused on teachers’ pedagogical reasoning. Codes were developed from the teachers’ statements and organized into categories of pedagogical opportunities, pedagogical and epistemic risks, and conditions of use. The findings indicated that teachers did not reject AI categorically; rather, they viewed it as a complementary tool whose value depended on teacher guidance, the mathematical accuracy and conceptual appropriateness of generated content, and alignment with instructional purposes. Lesson planning, individualized feedback, visualization, and time efficiency were identified as the main opportunities. Concerns included inaccurate content entering teaching and assessment, misconceptions, overreliance on ready-made answers, and reduced student participation in learning. Controlled use and teacher oversight were recurring criteria across different experience profiles. The study clarifies the subject-specific criteria mathematics teachers use when judging whether AI use is pedagogically acceptable.

items.title: MCF: A Memory- and Communication-Aware Co-Designed Framework for Long-Context LLM Inference
items.abstract: This paper presents Memory- and Communication-Aware Framework for Long-Context LLM Inference (MCF) that optimizes long-context inference through communication-aware and stage-adaptive KV-cache layout transitions. At the core of MCF is {Memory-Aware Replication and Scheduling} (MARS), a dynamic orchestration mechanism for chunked prefill. MARS exploits early-stage memory headroom by selectively replicating highly reused KV blocks, improving locality and hiding KV propagation latency behind attention computation. As prefill progresses and memory pressure increases, MARS progressively drains redundant replicas and converges the KV cache into a sharded decode-ready layout, avoiding expensive layout conversion at the prefill--decode boundary. For decoding, MCF adopts a query-centric execution model in which KV shards remain stationary while lightweight query tensors are routed across workers. This changes communication from KV-cache-dependent transfer to query-dependent transfer, reducing communication growth with context length. MCF further integrates a hardware-software co-designed execution layer based on an FPGA compute-NIC datapath, enabling metadata-driven KV routing and collective operations directly in the network path. Experiments show that MCF improves TTFT, throughput, and scalability over state-of-the-art distributed inference systems, with larger benefits as context length and cluster size increase.

items.abstract: Mechanistic interpretability seeks to explain how internal computations produce large language model behaviors, yet findings remain fragmented across methods and behavioral domains. We survey 229 papers across five behavior families: epistemic, linguistic, reasoning, safety, and social behaviors. We introduce a framework distinguishing five levels of mechanistic evidence, from decodability to generalization. Our cross-behavior synthesis reveals recurring mechanisms, distinctions between representation and causal control, and limitations of existing explanations. We conclude by identifying gaps in understanding computational roles, behavioral interactions, and generalization to interactive and agentic settings.

items.title: Media Hate as an Instigator of Information Warfare and Social Destabilization
items.abstract: This presentation examines media hate speech as an instrument of information warfare and a factor contributing to social destabilization, democratic erosion, and threats to national security, with particular attention to Russia's war against Ukraine. The presentation explores the role of hate speech in Russian information warfare, identifying three principal functions: the dehumanization of Ukrainians, the justification of military aggression, and the mobilization of public support for hostile policies. It examines how discriminatory narratives and hostile rhetoric circulate through traditional media, social networks, and digital communication platforms, including their international dissemination. Special attention is given to the manifestations of hate speech within Ukrainian society during wartime, including linguistic, religious, political, and social divisions. The presentation highlights the risks associated with polarization, the normalization of hostility, and the weakening of democratic culture. A substantial part of the analysis focuses on artificial intelligence and deepfake technologies as emerging instruments of information manipulation. Through international case studies, the presentation illustrates how synthetic media can impersonate political leaders, celebrities, journalists, and other public figures, facilitate disinformation campaigns, undermine public trust, and contribute to gender-based harassment. The presentation also examines regulatory responses, including the European Union's Artificial Intelligence Act, the Digital Services Act, and Denmark's proposed legal framework for protecting individuals against unauthorized digital imitations of their appearance and voice. The presentation concludes that effective responses to media hate and AI-enabled manipulation require an integrated approach combining legal safeguards, platform accountability, technological transparency, rapid intervention, media literacy, and public awareness. Particular emphasis is placed on protecting human dignity, democratic resilience, and fundamental rights in an increasingly AI-driven information environment.

items.title: Medical Embodied Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare Delivery and Clinical Workflows
items.abstract: Medical embodied artificial intelligence (AI) closes the loop between sensing, action and feedback in clinical and care tasks, from procedures and examination to rehabilitation and hospital logistics. Its clinical value therefore depends not only on what a system can do, but on how its action loop fits the task, the people who supervise it and the service responsible for recovery. In this structured narrative Review, we trace the field from image-guided and teleoperated robots to learned policies and foundation models, and survey its technical foundations along the action loop, from perception and task reasoning to planning, control, vision–language–action and world models and safety monitoring, together with data and simulation resources and applications across eight clinical task categories. A 96-source evidence map and targeted technical searches underpin the synthesis, and a separately defined subset of 40 direct empirical studies characterises the settings in which embodied systems have been validated. Evidence in this subset remains predominantly preclinical or feasibility-based and does not establish clinical superiority or long-term safety. We argue that the principal translational bottleneck is not insufficient autonomy alone but a mismatch among task boundaries, machine authority, evidence maturity and health-service readiness. To address this mismatch, we propose a task-bounded framework that links the operational design domain and allocated authority to the evidence required, the conditions for implementation and the mechanisms for monitoring, revalidation and rollback, and we identify technical priorities in grounded foundation models, shared data, uncertainty-aware autonomy and verifiable safety. The framework prioritises clinically relevant comparators, effective clinician takeover and evaluation of the complete workflow, including preparation, supervision and recovery, and offers a basis for appraising deployment claims; its decision value and effects on care now require prospective evaluation.

items.title: Mendel, a foundation model of human genetic variation, prioritizes regulatory variants and improves gene expression prediction
items.abstract: Abstract Human genome-wide association studies have identified hundreds of thousands of variant trait associations, but interpreting their mechanistic consequences at allele resolution remains a central bottleneck. DNA foundation models pretrained on genomic sequence corpora learn features predictive of regulatory activity, yet their training objectives are dominated by the conserved background common to all individuals, rather than the sparse variant sites at which human genetic variation is concentrated. Here we introduce Mendel, a DNA foundation model trained from scratch on human whole genome sequences using a variant-centric objective that concentrates supervision on allelic events within reference aligned sequence context. On held-out individuals, Mendel attains 0.984 micro-averaged SNV allele-prediction accuracy, compared with 0.311 for Evo 2. Mendel residual difficulty is selectively enriched at cis-eQTL variants, prioritizes fine-mapped causal variants (AUROC 0.731), where Evo 2 residuals performed near chance, and when converted into a cis-expression prior for modelling, improves prediction relative to an unweighted baseline in all 50 GTEx tissues.

items.title: Meninjau kembali pendidikan keperawatan di era generative AI: Implikasi terhadap pembelajaran, asesmen, dan kurikulum
items.abstract: Perkembangan Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) mulai mengubah cara mahasiswa belajar dan menghasilkan produk akademik dalam pendidikan keperawatan. Perubahan ini menimbulkan pertanyaan mengenai kompetensi yang perlu dibangun dan bukti pembelajaran yang perlu dihasilkan melalui asesmen. Kajian ini bertujuan meninjau kembali implikasi GenAI terhadap pendidikan keperawatan dengan mensintesis perubahan pembelajaran, asesmen, AI literacy, human judgment, serta kurikulum dan tata kelola. Kajian menggunakan integrative literature review dengan tahapan Whittemore dan Knafl. Penelusuran melalui Scopus untuk publikasi 2023–2026 menghasilkan 538 rekaman. Setelah pengelolaan duplikasi dan evaluasi literatur, 11 sumber ditetapkan sebagai core evidence dan 7 sebagai supporting literature. Analisis menghasilkan enam tema: perubahan cara belajar; efisiensi dan kedalaman belajar; redesain asesmen; AI literacy; human judgment; serta kurikulum dan tata kelola. Sintesis menunjukkan bahwa GenAI dapat memperluas interaksi dan efisiensi pembelajaran, tetapi tidak otomatis menghasilkan pembelajaran yang lebih mendalam. Karena itu, asesmen perlu semakin menampilkan reasoning, verifikasi, penerapan, komunikasi, dan performa. Integrasi GenAI dalam pendidikan keperawatan perlu diarahkan pada penguatan kompetensi profesional dan tanggung jawab manusia.

items.title: Mental Health of Students With Gifts and Talents in the Age of Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: With the global mental health care crisis (WHO, 2025), artificial intelligence (AI) tools are being explored as viable options for support. Their support for the mental health of students with gifts and talents (SWGT) is examined here. AI tools may be purpose-built for mental health support or companionship or designed for general assistance. The foundational large language model (LLM) for each of these is trained on different materials, which may not contain up-to-date information relevant to SWGT. SWGT should be educated on issues related to privacy and security, the possibility of false or misinformation from the AI tool, the prioritization of user engagement over helpful responding, and the dangers of overinvolvement. Talent development may be affected by the use of AI tools not trained to encourage psychosocial skills associated with success in the student’s domain of gifts or talents. Some controls are recommended to support SWGT’s positive use of AI.

items.title: Methodology for selecting an information source for online diagnostics of cutting tool edge condition
items.abstract: The work focuses on the development of a method for selecting diagnostic features in the milling of materials with significantly different properties. The use of two very different materials allowed for better generalization of the conclusions. The research concentrated on steel and composite materials, defined as combinations of two or more materials with diverse chemical and mechanical properties. A method for assessing the usefulness of measured physical quantities for predicting tool wear using machine learning techniques was proposed. Both vibration signals and cutting forces were considered, but the proposed method is general. The study implements artificial intelligence methods through the practical deployment of multiple machine‑learning models trained on vibration‑ and force‑based features. The methodology is based on a measure of the significance of data partitioning into subsets created from forces and vibration accelerations, combined with a large set of supervised machine learning methods, including classification and regression algorithms with various hyperparameters. This approach enables a relatively objective statistical assessment of the usefulness of a given physical quantity in monitoring tool condition.

items.title: Mixture-of-Quants: Hosting High-Precision LLMs at Low-Precision Memory Bandwidth
items.abstract: Serving a Large Language Model (LLM) to a single user is bound by memory bandwidth: every generated token requires the entire weight set to be read from memory. Quantising weights to 4 bits halves the traffic of an 8-bit model but measurably degrades reasoning. We propose Mixture-of-Quants (MoQ), which exploits the observation that at each decode step the difference between the 4-bit model's two highest token probabilities indicates whether the 8-bit weights would produce a different output. By default, MoQ decodes each new token at 4 bits. Only when the top-2 softmax margin falls below a threshold is the token recomputed from the 8-bit weights. The 8-bit weights are stored as the 4-bit plane plus a 4-bit residual, so the store is the same size as an 8-bit model but only 4 bits per weight are read on the majority of tokens. Across three 27B–31B parameter architectures and \(\approx\) 300,000 scored positions, the margin predicts 4-bit/8-bit disagreement with AUROC of 0.93–0.95, catching 80% of disagreements whilst escalating 12%–16% of positions. On 3,000 paired SuperGPQA questions with a 32,768-token reasoning budget, escalating 31% of tokens lifts accuracy from 57.2% (4-bit) to 58.9%, matching the 8-bit model (58.9%, exact McNemar \(p = 1.000\)) and beating 4-bit at the same significance as the 4-bit/8-bit gap itself (\(p = 0.010\)). By physically relocating weights between HBM3 (3,850 GB/s) and Grace LPDDR (84 GB/s) on GH200 superchips, we show MoQ's throughput advantage over 8-bit rises monotonically from 1.38\(\times\) to 1.70\(\times\) as bandwidth falls, and that placing the rarely-read residual plane in slow memory is 3.9\(\times\) faster than spreading the same bytes uniformly, a trade a flat 8-bit model cannot make.

items.abstract: The technology of Generative AI is now capable not only of writing, painting, and composing, but even transforming the work of others. While India's Copyright Act, 1957 was framed taking humans into consideration as the creators, yet there is an exception for Computer Generated Works and an additional set of Moral Rights provided for in Section 57. It contemplates that while the Copyright Act provides for a sufficient framework for the purpose, it lacks provisions regarding the role of humans in the creation, alteration by AI, misattribution, and proving the same. items.title: More Alerts, Less Prevention? A Computational Study of Hazard Detection, Response Capacity and Threshold Choice in Occupational Health and Safety
items.abstract: AI-enabled hazard detection is usually judged by whether it finds risky conditions. Prevention requires another step: somebody must have the time, authority and competence to respond. This article evaluates how that second step alters the interpretation of predictive safety performance. It reports a factorial computational experiment derived from a doctoral study of AI in occupational health and safety (OHS). Across 54 simulated operating conditions, five alert thresholds and 200 replications per condition, a score-based detector classifies 5,000 opportunities per replication. The design varies hazardous-opportunity prevalence (1%, 5% and 15%), score separation (1, 2 and 3), drift (0 and 0.75) and nominal response probability (0.40, 0.65 and 0.90), with response capacity limited to 500 alerts. At the reference threshold of 1.5, one 5%-prevalence, separation-2, no-drift condition yields mean residual hazardous opportunities of 180.8, 138.2 and 95.7 across the three response assumptions. With the same detector and nominal 65% response, imposing drift raises mean residual opportunities from 138.2 to 185.5. A sensitivity calculation also changes the preferred threshold when the relative weight of unresolved hazards and false alerts changes. The simulation shows why sensitivity, precision, workload and verified action belong in the same OHS decision model. All numerical data are computer-generated. The study does not report a deployed machine-learning system, workplace incidents, observed worker behaviour or injury reduction. Its contribution is a transparent stress test of the management choices that connect detection to prevention.

items.title: MOS: Towards Effective Smart Contract Vulnerability Detection through Mixture-of-Experts Tuning of Large Language Models
items.abstract: Smart contract vulnerabilities pose significant security risks to blockchain systems, potentially leading to severe financial losses. Existing methods face several limitations: (1) Program analysis-based approaches heavily rely on predefined patterns, lacking flexibility and adaptability to new vulnerability types; (2) Deep learning-based methods lack explanations for their detection results; (3) Large language model-based approaches suffer from high false positive rates. To address these challenges, we propose MOS, a smart contract vulnerability detection framework based on mixture-of-experts tuning (MOE-Tuning) of large language models. First, we conduct Continual Pre-training on a large-scale smart contract dataset to provide a domain-enhanced initialization for the subsequent MOE-Tuning process. Second, to provide reliable explanations for detected vulnerabilities, we construct a high-quality MOE-Tuning dataset through a multi-stage pipeline combining large language model generation and expert verification. Third, we design a vulnerability-aware routing mechanism that activates the most relevant expert networks by analyzing code features and their matching degree with experts, addressing the limitation of predefined patterns in program analysis approaches. Finally, we extend the feed-forward layers of the LLM after Continual Pre-training into multiple parallel expert networks, each specializing in specific vulnerability patterns. We also employ a dual-objective loss function: one for optimizing vulnerability detection and explanation performance, and another for balancing expert utilization through an auxiliary loss based on the scaled dot product of expert assignment frequencies and average routing probabilities, thereby improving model performance in complex vulnerability scenarios. Extensive experiments show that MOS consistently outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in four foundational and historically significant vulnerability types (Reentrancy, Timestamp, Integer Overflow/Underflow, Delegatecall) with average improvements of 6.38% in F1 score and 4.84% in accuracy. items.title: MSI-3, an improved version of the MSI application that includes both fungal and bacterial identifications for MALDI-ToF spectra
items.abstract: ABSTRACT Matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry (MALDI-ToF MS) is now central to routine diagnostics, enabling accurate identification of microbial species. We assessed the performance of MSI-3, the updated release of the free online mass spectrometry identification (MSI) platform that now supports bacterial, in addition to fungal, identification. MSI-3 was benchmarked against MSI-2 and the Bruker MALDI Biotyper using two fungal data sets: (i) a reference panel of 669 sequenced isolates (Panel 1), and (ii) a real-world set of user-submitted spectra (Panel 2). MSI-3 and MSI-2 demonstrated equivalent performance across all fungal groups in Panel 1, with 97.8% (mean of 892/912) concordance at the species or species complex level, and a massive added value compared to the Bruker database for filamentous fungi (from about 41% to about 98%). MSI-3 exhibited slightly longer identification times than MSI-2 (1.52 vs 0.84 s per spectrum), but remained compatible with real-time online usage. The increased identification time is offset by a twofold expansion of the reference database and algorithmic improvements. In Panel 2, MSI-3 achieved comparable performance to Bruker for bacterial and yeast spectra, and outperformed Bruker for filamentous fungi, especially Aspergillus spp., Fusarium spp., and dermatophytes. A new “uninterpretable” category was introduced in MSI-3 to flag potential mixed or poor-quality spectra, facilitating result interpretation. Overall, MSI-3 marks a substantial advance in the MSI platform, uniting flexibility, broad taxonomic coverage, and artificial intelligence (AI) readiness. Its combined use with Bruker enhances diagnostic performance, positioning MSI-3 as a powerful and scalable standard for microbial identification in clinical and research settings. IMPORTANCE This article highlights the major importance of MSI-3 as a significant advancement in microbial identification using matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry (MALDI-ToF MS). The expansion of the platform to bacterial identification, together with its already established fungal database and improved algorithms, now enables users to analyze mixed projects through a single workflow without additional sample handling or database switching. Used by more than 500 users worldwide, MSI-3 provides improved diagnostic performance, particularly for filamentous fungi, while offering a flexible and scalable solution for both clinical and research microbiology.

items.title: Multi-Horizon Future Discovery for Physics-Informed Exploration
items.abstract: Exploration in physical control environments requires agents to identify actions whose consequences reveal previously unexplored aspects of the underlying dynamics. However, many intrinsic motivation methods rely on immediate prediction errors, state novelty, or local physical changes, which may overlook informative outcomes that emerge across extended temporal horizons. We investigate whether learning structured representations of reachable futures can provide a more effective basis for exploration. To this end, we introduce Hamiltonian Temporal Contrastive Curiosity (HTC$^2$), a framework that combines multi-horizon temporal representation learning with Hamiltonian phase-space structure. A horizon-conditioned contrastive critic learns temporal relationships from future-state pairs sampled within the same episode. The distance between positive-pair representations is then used as an intrinsic reward, encouraging the agent to explore futures that remain insufficiently organized in the learned representation. To incorporate information about physical dynamics, we additionally modulate this reward using bounded multi-step Hamiltonian variation, rather than directly rewarding changes in the Hamiltonian itself. We integrate HTC$^2$ with both Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) and Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), and evaluate it across six DeepMind Control Suite tasks. Comparisons with ICM, RIDE, E3B, Plan2Explore, and a single-step Hamiltonian curiosity baseline are complemented by state-coverage evaluations, component ablations, and phase-space diagnostics to characterize the contributions of temporal learning and physical structure to exploratory behavior.

items.title: Multilingual Artificial Intelligence for Classifying Ethiopian FinTech User Reviews
items.abstract: Abstract The rapid expansion of mobile and digital financial services in Ethiopia has generated substantial user feedback, yet automated analysis remains challenging because reviews are multilingual, informal, code-switched, and weakly represented in existing language resources. This study develops and evaluates a reproducible multilingual natural language processing framework for classifying Ethiopian FinTech reviews into five service-oriented categories: General Praise or Suggestions (GPS), User Experience and Design Issues (UXD), Transaction and Payment Failures (TPF), Login and Authentication Problems (LAP), and Service and Support Complaints (SSC). An annotated corpus was constructed from publicly accessible reviews associated with 27 Ethiopian FinTech applications. The initial collection contained 8,387 records, of which 7,148 were retained after quality-control procedures. The corpus contains English, Amharic, and English-Amharic code-switched reviews. We benchmark conventional TF-IDF classifiers, neural architectures, and multilingual/African-language transformer models under a leakage-controlled experimental protocol in which random oversampling is restricted to the training partition. Using five-fold stratified cross-validation, repeated random seeds, held-out evaluation, confidence intervals, and paired bootstrap significance testing, AfroXLMR achieved the strongest performance, with 96.7% accuracy and 96.0% macro-F1, followed by AfriBERTa (96.5%, 95.8%) and XLM-R (96.2%, 95.4%). The strongest neural baseline, CNN, achieved 95.1% accuracy and 94.3% macro-F1, while XGBoost achieved 90.2% accuracy and 88.1% macro-F1. Minority-class recall improved substantially after training-only oversampling. Language-specific analysis indicated lower performance for English-Amharic code-switched reviews than for English and Amharic reviews. These findings illustrate the value of contextual multilingual representations while also demonstrating that data imbalance, linguistic variation, short reviews, and resource constraints remain important limitations. The study contributes a documented Ethiopian FinTech review corpus and a comparative methodological framework for low-resource multilingual financial-service text classification.

items.title: Multiproperty optimization of therapeutic antibodies through sequence editing via large language model and reinforcement learning
items.abstract: Discovering antibodies with multiple beneficial properties is essential for therapeutic drug development, but experimentally identified antibodies require further optimization. Joint optimization remains challenging because sequence space is vast, annotations are sparse and property tradeoffs are common. Herein, we propose AbOptimizer, a reinforcement learning framework for multiproperty antibody optimization through parallel multisite sequence editing. AbOptimizer identifies promising editing sites and edit actions, including ‘reservation’, ‘substitution’ and optional ‘insertion’ or ‘deletion’, before recommending mutations from protein language models, while surrogate evaluation and Pareto rewards shape policy training. We evaluate AbOptimizer on three therapeutic antibodies across multiproperty, data-limited and indel-inclusive optimization. In silico, AbOptimizer improves optimized properties and outperforms baseline methods. In vitro, selected variants show affinity-specificity co-optimization for emibetuzumab, improved affinity and specificity with largely maintained thermal stability for siltuximab, and indel-inclusive affinity optimization for trastuzumab. These results validate AbOptimizer as a practical framework for therapeutic antibody optimization. This study presents AbOptimizer, a computational framework that edits antibody sequences to improve multiple therapeutic properties. Tests on three antibodies show improved affinity, specificity and stability-related profiles.
